test_title: PYST 8: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 01 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question:
Fill in the blank:
Direct taxes are collected by the government from ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Individuals and companies**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Direct taxes** are defined as taxes that are paid directly to the **government** by the person or organization on whom they are levied. In this system, the **tax liability** and the **tax burden** fall on the same entity, meaning the tax cannot be shifted to another person.

• **Individuals** are a primary source of direct tax collection through **Income Tax**. Every individual whose income exceeds the basic **exemption limit** is required to pay tax to the **Central Government**. **Hence, this part of the option is correct.**

• **Companies** (both domestic and foreign) contribute to direct taxes through **Corporate Tax**. This tax is calculated on the **net profit** earned by the company during a **financial year**. **Hence, this part of the option is correct.**

• **Importers** are generally associated with **Customs Duty**, which is an **indirect tax**. The burden of customs duty is usually passed on to the end consumer by including it in the price of the imported goods. **Hence, option 2 is incorrect.**

• **Consumers** primarily pay **indirect taxes** such as **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** or **Value Added Tax (VAT)**. While they bear the ultimate burden, they do not pay it directly to the government; instead, it is collected by **traders** or service providers. **Hence, option 3 is incorrect.**

• **Traders** act as intermediaries who collect **indirect taxes** from consumers and remit them to the government. While traders pay **income tax** on their personal or business profits, the broad category for direct tax collection is defined by the legal status of **Individuals and companies**. **Hence, option 4 is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** is the apex body in **India** responsible for the administration of direct tax laws. It is a **statutory authority** functioning under the **Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963**, and is part of the **Department of Revenue** in the **Ministry of Finance**.

• **Progressive Taxation**: Direct taxes in **India** are **progressive** in nature. This means that the **tax rate** increases as the **taxpayer's income** increases, which helps in **reducing wealth disparity** and ensuring **social equity**.

• **Income Tax Act, 1961**: This is the primary legislation that provides the legal framework for **levying**, **collecting**, and **recovering** income tax. It contains various **sections** that define **taxable income**, **deductions** (like **Section 80C**), and **exemptions**.

• **Types of Direct Taxes**: Beyond **Income Tax** and **Corporate Tax**, other examples include **Capital Gains Tax** (levied on the sale of assets like **property** or **stocks**) and **Securities Transaction Tax (STT)** (levied on transactions in the **stock market**).

• **Economic Stability**: Direct taxes serve as an **automatic stabilizer** for the economy. During periods of **inflation**, higher **income levels** lead to higher tax collections, which helps in **mopping up excess liquidity** from the market.

**Important Points__**

• **Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)**: This is a system where the person responsible for making a payment (like **salary**, **rent**, or **professional fees**) deducts a certain percentage of tax before paying the balance to the **individual** or **company**. It ensures a **steady flow of revenue** to the government.

• **Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT)**: Under **Section 115JB**, MAT is levied on **zero-tax companies** that show significant **book profits** but pay little to no tax due to various **exemptions** and **incentives**. This ensures that every **profitable company** contributes to the **national exchequer**.

• **Direct Tax-to-GDP Ratio**: This is a critical **economic indicator**. A rising ratio suggests that the **tax base** is expanding and the **tax administration** is becoming more **efficient**. In **India**, the government aims to increase this ratio to fund **infrastructure** and **social welfare schemes**.

• **Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA)**: **India** has entered into **DTAAs** with over **80 countries** to ensure that **taxpayers** do not have to pay **direct tax** on the same income in two different **jurisdictions**, thereby promoting **foreign investment**.

• **Abolition of Wealth Tax**: It is noteworthy that **Wealth Tax** was abolished in **India** starting from the **2015-16 financial year**. It was replaced by a **surcharge** on **super-rich** individuals earning more than **1 crore** rupees annually.
